keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Great Prussian Uprising 'began on 20 September 1260'; Sambians, Natangians, Bartians, Warmians and Pogesanians rose, Pomesanians did not. At the low point the Order kept only 'strongholds in Balga, Elbing, Culm, Thorn, and Königsberg', which the contest events show as disputed. Heilsberg fell in 1274; the page dates the central tribes' surrender to 1277. Revision after review: the lands lost in 1253 and 1255 (Sambia, Natangia, Bartia, Warmia, Pogesania) come back to the rising by a gain event of 20 September 1260 and return to the Order in 1277; Galindia (Masuria) is not mentioned in the page's account of the rising and stays with the Order; Nadruvia, Skalvia and Sudovia were free throughout (the page says the Sudovians under Skomantas supported the rising; it does not say Nadruvia or Skalvia rose). Nadruvia is now named in the shape, because subtracting Masuria had clipped 4 of its cells.

ledger.note: 997: the first dated event on Prussian land: Adalbert of Prague slain among the Prussians. 'Adalbert was slain in 997 during a missionary effort to Christianise the Prussians.' The tribes were older (Tacitus's Aesti in 98 CE is only a suggestion; the Bavarian Geographer's Brus in the ninth century is undated); no state was founded.

1233: the Order founds Marienwerder in Pomesania. 'Marienwerder (Kwidzyn) was founded in Pomesania by an army of 10,000' in summer 1233; the Pogesanians were routed on the frozen Sirgune in the winter of 1233-34.
1236: Pomesania submits. 'With Margrave Henry III of Meissen's support, most Pomesanians submitted.' The Pomesanians stayed out of the 1260 uprising.
1236: the fighting for Pomesania ends with the submission.

The revolt 'began on 20 September 1260'; the page says the Prussians took most Teutonic castles (placing the fall of most in 1262-1263) and that 'the Knights were left only with strongholds in Balga, Elbing, Culm, Thorn, and Königsberg'. ledger.note: 1277: the lands the risings had retaken pass back to the Order. The Natangians and Warmians 'accepted baptism and promised their loyalty to the Knights' (Great Prussian Uprising page); Heilsberg, the rebels' headquarters, fell in 1274 and the Pogesanians alone fought on and were crushed. The same page has Sambia 'abandoned the fight' after a decisive battle in 1265; the dossier keeps Samland in the shape to 1276 because the page gives no border for it and the Order held Balga and Königsberg throughout. Later revolts in 1286 and 1295 changed no border.

wars.outcome: Teutonic Order victory: the Prussian tribes were conquered between 1233 and 1283; the Order held Prussia by the end of the 13th century.
wars.note: The page's infobox gives the crusade as 1217-1274; the Old Prussians page says the conquest ended in 1283 and the war with the Lithuanians began. The dossier uses 1230 (the Order's campaigns from Culmerland) to 1283.

wars.name: First Prussian Uprising
wars.outcome: The Order kept the land: the Prussians beat it at Rensen (1244) and Krücken (November 1249) but lacked siege capability; Swantopelk of Pomerelia stopped aiding them in 1248; the Treaty of Christburg was signed in February 1249.
wars.note: The Great Prussian Uprising page dates this first uprising 1242-1249, 'sometimes dated to 1253'.

notes: Old Prussians are a tribal area, not a state: the Old Prussians page says the tribes 'never formed a common political and territorial organisation' (no capital; capitals is empty). Start 997 is the first page-dated event on their land (Adalbert), not a founding. Disagreement with the teutonic-order dossier: that dossier dates the gain of Warmia, Natangia and Bartia to February 1249 (Christburg) and the central tribes to 1277; this dossier ends the first uprising in 1253 because the Prussian Crusade page has fighting to 1253, so the orchestrator may align the two. Pomesania is 1236 in both. Sudovians (Yotvingians) are kept inside this dossier because the Old Prussians page calls them 'sometimes' a Prussian tribe; the Yotvingians page has no conquest date. Skalvia and Nadruvia: no page opened gives a conquest year (1274-1283 only). Culm (Chełmno) land, granted to the Order in 1226/1230, is outside the shape: the page lists it among Peter of Dusburg's lands but it was Masovian by then. Region coordinates for Pomesania and Sudovia are circles because the gazetteer lacks Kwidzyn and Suwałki (gazetteer_names_needed). No area comparison possible (no infobox area).
